edges.description: Failed SECISBP2-dependent Sec incorporation reduces synthesis of multiple human selenoproteins.
Reduced synthesis of deiodinase selenoproteins disrupts thyroid hormone activation and inactivation.
Deficiency of antioxidant selenoproteins increases cellular reactive oxygen species and stress sensitivity.

nodes.description: Deiodinases are selenoproteins required for thyroid hormone metabolism. Their reduced activity produces the characteristic abnormal thyroid function tests observed in SECISBP2 deficiency.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in SECISBP2 result in abnormal thyroid hormone metabolism.
evidence.snippet: Deiodinases (DIOs) are selenoproteins involved in thyroid hormone metabolism.

nodes.description: Loss of antioxidant selenoprotein capacity increases cellular reactive oxygen species and vulnerability to oxidative injury.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the selenocysteine insertion sequence-binding protein 2 gene lead to a multisystem selenoprotein deficiency disorder in humans.
evidence.snippet: Cutaneous deficiencies of antioxidant selenoenzymes, increased cellular ROS, and susceptibility to ultraviolet radiation-induced oxidative damage may mediate the observed photosensitivity.

nodes.description: Decreased Sec insertion reduces synthesis of multiple selenoproteins, including deiodinases and antioxidant enzymes, creating a multisystem selenoprotein deficiency state.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the selenocysteine insertion sequence-binding protein 2 gene lead to a multisystem selenoprotein deficiency disorder in humans.
evidence.snippet: These individuals have reduced synthesis of most of the 25 known human selenoproteins, resulting in a complex phenotype.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in SECISBP2 result in abnormal thyroid hormone metabolism.
evidence.snippet: An unrelated child with a similar phenotype was compound heterozygous with respect to mutations in SECISBP2.

evidence.reference_title: Novel compound heterozygous mutations in the SBP2 gene: characteristic clinical manifestations and the implications of GH and triiodothyronine in longitudinal bone growth and maturation.
evidence.snippet: The patient showed typical symptoms of SBP2 deficiency, and novel compound heterozygous mutations were identified in SBP2 (p.M515fsX563/p.Q79X).

nodes.description: SECISBP2/SBP2 loss impairs SECIS-mediated recoding of UGA as selenocysteine, creating a proximal defect in selenocysteine incorporation during translation.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in SECISBP2 result in abnormal thyroid hormone metabolism.
evidence.snippet: Systematic linkage analysis of genes involved in DIO2 synthesis and degradation led to the identification of an inherited Sec incorporation defect, caused by a homozygous missense mutation in SECISBP2 (also called SBP2).
